summary: Name the GDExtension library by the architecture of the host that builds it -- tools/build-native-bridge.sh from uname -m (aarch64 mapped to arm64) and tools/build-native-bridge.ps1 from the Windows processor architecture -- and repair every path that named the hard-coded x86_64 file: the macos arm64 rows in game/bin/project42_sim.gdextension, the macOS preset's universal binary_format and both architectures' dylibs in its include_filter, and the host-architecture assertions in verify.yml and nightly.yml. The end of it is E10's macOS job exporting and uploading a macOS artifact whose zip carries the dylib at the path Godot resolves.

coordination.notes: E10 recorded two blockers in game/ and refused to fake around them; this lane fixes them at their root, which is the build script's hard-coded x86_64 file name rather than the .gdextension alone. game/export_presets.cfg is touched on the macOS preset lines only (binary_format/architecture and include_filter); verify.yml on its library assertion step only. Nothing under godot-rust/src, game/scripts, content or docs/SHIP_PLAN.md. One path outside the card's Touches list: game/project.godot gains rendering/textures/vram_compression/import_etc2_astc=true, because Godot refuses a universal or arm64 macOS export while it is off and universal is the only macOS binary format the official template archive ships. No active claim held that file. It is one line under [rendering], additive, and changes no renderer behaviour.

checks: The defect, named exactly: tools/build-native-bridge.sh read `uname -m` for nothing and wrote project42_sim.<platform>.expedition_v5_<config>.x86_64.<ext> on every host. It now maps uname -m to Godot's token (x86_64|amd64 -> x86_64, aarch64|arm64 -> arm64, anything else refused) and names the installed file with it; tools/build-native-bridge.ps1 does the same on Windows from [System.Runtime.InteropServices.RuntimeInformation]::OSArchitecture (X64 -> x86_64, Arm64 -> arm64, anything else throws): passed

Blocker 1 of E10's two, fixed: game/bin/project42_sim.gdextension declares macos.debug.arm64 and macos.release.arm64 beside the x86_64 rows (and the same arm64 pair for linux and windows, so no host the build script now supports can produce a file no row names). Run 34031556245's assertion checked both macOS release rows and both files and passed: passed

Blocker 2 of E10's two, fixed: game/export_presets.cfg's macOS preset sets binary_format/architecture="universal" -- the only macOS binary format the official template archive can satisfy, as E10 established from the archive itself -- and its include_filter lists both architectures' debug and release dylibs: passed

Blocker 3, found here and not in E10's list, in a file outside this card's stated Touches: run 34030138603 got past the .gdextension and refused at the export with "ERROR: Cannot export project with preset \"macOS\" due to configuration errors: Cannot export for universal or arm64 if ETC2 ASTC texture format is disabled. Enable it in the Project Settings (Rendering > Textures > VRAM Compression > Import ETC2 ASTC)." followed by "ERROR: Project export for preset \"macOS\" failed." game/project.godot gained one line under [rendering], textures/vram_compression/import_etc2_astc=true. No active claim held that file; it is additive and changes no renderer behaviour, only adding an ETC2/ASTC copy at import time: passed

Blocker 4, the one that made this card more than a rename. With universal set and the arm64 rows in place, run 34030691308 exported, wrote the .app, exited zero and left the simulation out of it. Run 34031119836's export log says why, verbatim: "ERROR: Failed to open '/Users/runner/work/project-42-pirate-island-rpg/project-42-pirate-island-rpg/game/bin/macos/project42_sim.macos.expedition_v5_release.x86_64.dylib'." / "   at: copy (core/io/dir_access.cpp:426)". A universal macOS export copies the library declared for EVERY architecture, not the host's alone, so reordering the rows could not help and did not (that was run 34031119836's own change). tools/build-native-bridge.sh now builds both macOS architectures, the second by cross-compiling to x86_64-apple-darwin, and the resulting .app is universal in the library as well as the engine binary: passed
